Done — Suspense is clean for March. Summary:

**All six charges cleared, $3,134.85 total:**

| Merchant | Amount | Coded to |
|---|---|---|
| Delta Air Lines | 642.18 | 6300 Travel |
| Marriott Chicago | 418.90 | 6300 Travel |
| Blue Plate Bistro | 186.45 | 6310 Meals & Entertainment |
| Figma | 540.00 | 6200 Software Subscriptions |
| Staples | 97.32 | 6600 Office Supplies |
| LinkedIn Ads | 1,250.00 | 6410 Advertising |

**2900 Suspense is now $0.00** — both March activity and cumulative ending balance.

A few judgment calls worth your attention:

- **Figma → expense, not prepaid.** It's a single-month Organization plan, so Policy 4's prepaid treatment doesn't apply (and it's under the $1,000 threshold anyway).
- **Blue Plate Bistro → 6310, not Travel.** The receipt shows a client dinner with 4 external guests from Corvid Retail, which is entertainment rather than employee travel.
- **LinkedIn → 6410 Advertising, not 6400 Marketing Programs**, since it's paid media spend.

Two things I did beyond the strict ask: I attached the receipts to the **original bank-feed entries** as well (they'd been posted by the feed with zero documentation, which fails Policy 2), and I verified each receipt amount ties exactly to its charge — no variances, so no exceptions to flag.

One item to carry into the bank rec: these card charges **don't appear as individual lines** on the March GL 1000 statement — the card evidently settles as one consolidated payment. So whoever picks up the bank reconciliation should expect an aggregate settlement rather than six discrete lines. I left all checklist items untouched since this work was only a slice of the open close tasks.
